Hon'ble Shri Justice Narendra Kumar Vyas Order on Board 08/10/2024 1.

This is the first bail application filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of regular bail to the applicant, who has been arrested on 22.05.2024 in connection with Crime No. 114/2023, registered at Police Station- Gariyaband, District- Gariyaband (C.G.) for the offence punishable under Sections 366, 376 (2)(n) of I.P.C. & Section 4/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012

sentences.text: 2. Case of the prosecution in brief is that on 24.04.2024 victim's father lodged a complaint before the police station alleging that his minor daughter had gone to school and did not returned back to home, therefore, a missing person report was lodged by the police.
The victim came back to home and stated that the applicant took her to Hyderabad and made forcefully physical relationship with her on pretext of marriage.
On the basis of the statement of the victim, the offence as aforestated has been registered against the applicant.

3. sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
He would further submit that there was love affair between the applicant and the victim and she has not supported case of the prosecution.
The victim was not minor on the date of incident and physical relationship was made with her consent.

He would further submit that the applicant is in jail since 22.05.2024, the trial is likely to take some time for its final disposal,
therefore, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application and would submit that there is sufficient material available in the case diary against the applicant regarding commission of offence.

He would further submit that the victim is aged below 18 years, therefore,
the consent given by the victim, cannot be considered while granting bail to the applicant.

Hence,
the application for grant of bail may be rejected.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

7. Considering the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. as well as court statement particulary at paragraph No. 5 & 6 has not supported case of the prosecution and also considering that the applicant is in jail since 22.05.2024 and the conclusion of the trial may take some time, without commenting anything on merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a fit case to grant bail to the applicant.
8. Accordingly, the bail application filed under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs. 25,000/-
with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial court.
He shall appear before the trial court on each and every date given by the said trial court, till disposal of the trial.
Certified copy as per rules.
